Contact VISN15EDRP@va.gov, the EDRP Coordinator for questions/assistance.

Learn more Pay: Competitive salary, annual performance bonus, regular salary increases Paid Time Off: 50-55 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year and possible 5 day paid absence for CME) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory CME: Possible $1,000 per year reimbursement (must be full-time with board certification) Malpractice: Free liability protection with tail coverage provided Contract: No Physician Employment Contract and no significant restriction on moonlighting Robert J Dole VA Medical Center is hiring a full time Urologist to serve Veteran patients of the facility.

The incumbent may be asked to provide care in various settings to include outpatient clinics, inpatient units such as Intensive Care and Med/Surg, and in the Emergency Department.

The duties and responsibilities includes, but are not limited to, the following: Provide direct patient care to patients and clinical guidance to mid-level providers in the Urology section Participate in the progressive improvement of the service delivery, which may include programmatic participation in initiatives within the facility Responsible for all aspects of medical care and provide or assist residents and/or the mid-level practitioner in the process of evaluation and treatment of the Urology patients Evaluate the patient to assess changes in the physical and mental status.

A progress note is written in the patient's chart Coordinate with providers within their own and outside of their own Service Line, and with other VHA facilities or community providers as determined by the plan of care for the veteran Ultimately responsible to ensure barriers for Veterans and staff are minimized in order to promote a positive work environment.

Fosters positive working relationships with staff, peers and Veterans Perform consultations within their own and other service lines as indicated Responsible for the provision of clinical care, graduate and undergraduate medical education, and scientific research as appropriate Although on-call hours are seldom, staff within Urology service shall be available for emergency interventions Work Schedule: 8:00 am - 4:30 pm, Monday - Friday
To qualify for this position, you must meet the basic requirements as well as any additional requirements (if applicable) listed in the job announcement. Applicants pending the completion of training or license requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met.

Currently employed physician(s) in VA who met the requirements for appointment under the previous qualification standard at the time of their initial appointment are deemed to have met the basic requirements of the occupation.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Degree of doctor of medicine or an equivalent degree resulting from a course of education in allopathic medicine or osteopathic medicine.

The degree must have been obtained from one of the schools approved by the Department of Veterans Affairs for the year in which the course of study was completed. Current, full and unrestricted license to practice medicine or surgery in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Residency Training: Physicians must have completed residency training, approved by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in an accredited core specialty training program leading to eligibility for board certification.

(NOTE: VA physicians involved in academic training programs may be required to be board certified for faculty status.) Approved residencies are: (1) Those approved by the accrediting bodies for graduate medical education, the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA), in the list published for the year the residency, or fellowship if applicable, was completed; OR (2) One year of post medical school training (internship, first year of residency, or transitional year residency) approved by ACGME or AOA followed by two years of post-training independent practice (performing under a full and unrestricted license) in the United States; OR (3) Non-US residency training programs followed by a minimum of three years of verified independent practice in the United States (performing under a full and unrestricted license) performing duties related to the position they are applying for (United States fellowships would be creditable towards this requirement), which the local Medical Staff Executive Committee deems to have provided the applicant with appropriate professional training and believes has exposed the Physician to an appropriate range of patient care experiences.

Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis. PRPs are not considered independent practitioners and will not be privileged; rather, they are to have a "scope of practice" that allows them to perform certain restricted duties under supervision.

Additionally, surgery residents in gap years may also be appointed as PRPs.

In rare and unusual circumstances, the Facility Director can submit a memo to the VISN Director through the VISN Chief Medical Officer, who may approve requests for reasonable exceptions to the residency training requirement for Physicians whose composite record of experience, accomplishments, performance, and qualifications warrant such action.

Proficiency in spoken and written English. Preferred Experience: Robotic surgery Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/.

Physical Requirements: Light lifting, under 15 pounds, light carrying under 15 pounds, pulling hand over hand 1.5 hours (varies), pushing, 1 hour (varies), reaching above shoulders, use of fingers, walking (6 hours- varies), standing (8 hours- varies), repeated bending (4 hours varies), use of hands and fingers, ability for rapid mental and muscular coordination simultaneously, near vision correctable at 12" to 16" Jaeger 1 to 4, hearing (aid permitted).

Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and experience requirements described below.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document.

Basic Requirement for Supervisory Physician (Clinical Director): Degree: Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine, or equivalent from a school in the United States or Canada.

This degree must have been accredited by the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association; Association of American Medical Colleges; Liaison Committee on Medical Education; Commission on Osteopathic College Accreditation of the American Osteopathic Association, or an accrediting body recognized by the U.S.

Department of Education at the time the degree was obtained. A Doctor of Medicine or equivalent degree from a foreign medical school must have provided education and medical knowledge equivalent to accredited schools in the United States.

Evidence of equivalency to accredited schools in the United States is demonstrated by permanent certification by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates, a fifth pathway certificate for Americans who completed premedical education in the United States and graduate education in a foreign country, or successful completion of the U.S.

Medical Licensing Examination.

(Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts or proof of foreign equivalency with your application package.) Licensure: Applicants must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration as a Physician from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States.

Graduate Training: Subsequent to obtaining a Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree, a candidate must have had at least one year of supervised experience providing direct service in a clinical setting, i.e., a one-year internship or the first year of a residency program in a hospital or an institution accredited for such training.

In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Residency Training: Applicants must have successfully completed the required accredited residency training in the specialty of the position to be filled or equivalent experience and training equal to at least 5 years.

Experience may not be substituted for residency training that is required for the specialty identified. If you are selected for a Physician position: A salary quote will not be provided to you at the time of the initial job offer. The salary determination process begins after the initial job offer is accepted.

This consists of the Activity Compensation Panel adding base pay and market pay to determine your starting salary and this will be provided to you once approved. Salary for physician positions is based on a tier scale, determined by the position specialty, grade, and location.

*Die Universitätsklinik für Dermatologie verfügt über einen stationären Bereich und eine grosse Ambulanz mit zahlreichen Spezialsprechstunden, inkl. Hauttumorzentrum und Chirurgie. Die Dermatopathologie als Bindeglied zwischen Diagnostik, Behandlung, Lehre und Forschung stellt einen strategisch wichtigen medizinischen Schwerpunkt der Klinik dar.*
## **Das erwartet Sie** ##
* Enge Teamarbeit unter Dermatopatholog:innen/Patholog:innen und mit Kliniker:innen.
* Eigenverantwortliche Diagnostik im gesamten Spektrum der dermatologischen Histopathologie.
* Wöchentliche Vorstellung histologischer Präparate bei klinisch-pathologischen Diskussionen, sowie in Zusammenarbeit mit Hauttumorboard.
* Kontinuierliche Anpassung des Leistungs- und Service- Angebotes.
* Initiierung, Leitung und Unterstützung von Forschungsprojekten unter Einbeziehung der Dermatopathologie.
* Beteiligung an der Lehre, Fort- und Weiterbildung.
## **Das bringen Sie mit** ##
* Fachärztin:arzt für Dermatologie mit abgeschlossener Weiterbildung / Schwerpunkt Dermatopathologie oder Fachärztin:arzt für Pathologie mit profunder Expertise in Dermatopathologie.
* Sie haben das Diplom für Dermatologie in Frankfurt (ICDP - UEMS International Board Certification in Dermatopathology) bereits erworben oder werden dies in Kürze tun.
* Sie haben Freude an der Morphologie und möchten an unserer Klinik für eine qualitativ hochstehende Dermatopathologie verantwortlich sein.
* Anwendung von molekularpathologischer Diagnostik für dermatologische, dermatopathologische und dermatopädiatrische Fragestellungen.
* Sie zeigen Interesse an akademischer Dermatologie und verfolgen eine eigene Forschungstätigkeit.
* Sie denken und handeln flexibel, arbeiten selbständig und sind belastbar.
* Sie kommunizieren stilsicher in Deutsch (mündlich und schriftlich), Kenntnisse der französischen Sprache sind von Vorteil.
## **Unser Angebot** ##
* In unserem akkreditierten Dermatopathologie-Labor werden jährlich 20'000 Präparate der Haut aufgearbeitet und begutachtet. Unser Angebot umfasst Routineuntersuchungen an Paraffin-fixiertem Material und Gefrierschnitten (Mohs Chirurgie) sowie eine grosse Palette (immun-)histochemischer Untersuchungen.
* Daneben besteht eine enge Zusammenarbeit mit dem der Pathologie der Universität Bern, das als Betreiber des Clinical Genomics Laboratory des Inselspitals auch umfassende molekularpathologische Diagnostik anbietet.
* Unser Histologie-Labor ist zudem als ICDP-Trainingszentrum anerkannt und bemüht sich um Förderung des beruflichen Nachwuchses.
* Wir bieten Ihnen eine spannende und abwechslungsreiche abwechslungsreiche Position in einem innovativen, interdisziplinären Umfeld mit kollegial wertschätzendem und freundlichen Arbeitsklima. Es bestehen zudem interessante akademische Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten. Ausserdem bieten wir an, dass Sie selbst klinisch tätig sein können.

Die Universitätsklinik für Dermatologie des Inselspitals Bern zählt zu den führenden Hautkliniken der Schweiz. Mit einem breiten Spektrum an Spezialsprechstunden, einem renommierten Hauttumorzentrum und einer engen Verzahnung von Klinik, Forschung und Lehre bieten wir ein dermatologisches Umfeld, das seinesgleichen sucht.

Die Allgemeine Dermatologie bildet das klinische Rückgrat dieser Klinik und ist strategisch der Ort, an dem Breite und Tiefe zusammenkommen: Hier wird das volle Spektrum dermatologischer Erkrankungen ambulant betreut \- von entzündlichen Systemerkrankungen über seltene Genodermatosen bis hin zu Hauttumoren \-, hier laufen die Fäden der Spezialdisziplinen zusammen, und hier entsteht der klinische Mehrwert, der eine Universitätsklinik von anderen unterscheidet.

Für diese Schlüsselposition suchen wir eine fachlich versierte, engagierte Persönlichkeit, die die Allgemeine Dermatologie mit Überzeugung verkörpert.
Das erwartet Sie
Eigenverantwortliche Patientenbetreuung in den allgemeindermatologischen Sprechstunden \- von der Erstdiagnose bis zur Langzeitbetreuung komplexer Verläufe.
Beurteilung und Behandlung des gesamten dermatologischen Krankheitsspektrums: entzündliche Erkrankungen (Psoriasis, atopische Dermatitis, Autoimmundermatosen), Infektionsdermatologie, Hauttumoren und seltene Dermatosen.
Systemische Therapieführung inkl. Biologika und Small Molecules bei immunvermittelten Hauterkrankungen.
Enge interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit innerhalb der Klinik mit Spezialsprechstunden, Hauttumorzentrum und Dermatopathologie, sowie mit Partnerdisziplinen des Inselspitals.
Mitbetreuung und Supervision von Assistenzärzt:innen sowie Engagement in der studentischen Lehre.
Beteiligung an klinischer Forschung und Möglichkeit zur Entwicklung eigener wissenschaftlicher Projekte.
Teilnahme an klinischen Studien und interdisziplinären Fallkonferenzen.
Das bringen Sie mit
Facharzttitel FMH für Dermatologie und Venerologie.
Breite klinische Erfahrung in der allgemeinen Dermatologie und Freude an der Vielfalt des Faches.
Sicherer Umgang mit systemischen Therapien und Biologika bei entzündlichen Hauterkrankungen.
Ausgeprägte Patientenorientierung und Freude an der langfristigen, vertrauensvollen Betreuung.
Interesse an Lehre, Weiterbildung und Mitbetreuung junger Kolleg:innen.
Wissenschaftliches Interesse und Bereitschaft zur Beteiligung an Forschung und klinischen Studien.
Stilsicheres Deutsch und Englisch in Wort und Schrift sowie gute Kenntnisse der ösischen Sprache (oder Bereitschaft, diese rasch zu erwerben)
Kollegiales, empathisches Auftreten und Freude an der Arbeit in einem grossen, interdisziplinären Team.
Unser Angebot
Aussergewöhnliche Fallvielfalt: seltene Erkrankungen, komplexe Verläufe und ein Patientenkollektiv von Universitätsniveau.
Vollständige Einbettung in eine führende Klinik mit Hauttumorzentrum, Dermatopathologie, Dermatochirurgie und spezialisierten Sprechstunden \- kurze Wege, direkte Kollegialität.
Zugang zu modernster Diagnostik und einem breiten Biologika\- und Systemtherapie\-Portfolio.
Akademische Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten: Forschungsprojekte, internationale Kongressteilnahme, Habilitation möglich.
Strukturiertes Weiterbildungsumfeld mit aktivem Austausch, Fallkonferenzen und Supervision.
Attraktive Anstellungsbedingungen (Personalrestaurant, Kindertagesstätte, Weiterbildungszeit).
Standort Bern: hohe Lebensqualität, exzellente Verkehrsanbindung, internationales Umfeld.

**Position:** Assistenzarzt/-ärztin

Bäretswil liegt im Zürcher Oberland und besticht durch seine attraktive Lage zwischen Stadt und Natur. Die Region ist durch die S-Bahn und gut ausgebaute Straßen an Zürich angebunden, wodurch Pendler schnell ins Zentrum gelangen. Sie profitieren von modernen Unternehmen, einem innovativen Wirtschaftsumfeld und gleichzeitig von der hohen Lebensqualität eines ländlichen Standorts mit vielfältigen Freizeitangeboten.
### Ihr Wirkungsfeld als Assistenzarzt in Bäretswil
· Untersuchung, Diagnostik sowie Therapieplanung unter Supervision
· Dabei tägliche Visiten und Betreuung der eigenen Patientinnen
· Verordnungen, Berichte sowie Austrittsplanung verantworten

### Damit überzeugen Sie uns

### Ihr Arbeitsumfeld: Ihre neue Wirkungsstätte
Sie arbeiten in einer etablierten Institution im Gesundheitswesen – mit einem eingespielten Team, klaren Abläufen und echter Wertschätzung. Wichtig für diese Stelle: Allgemeine Innere Medizin. Dabei erwartet Sie ein Umfeld, in dem Fachlichkeit und Menschlichkeit zusammengehören.

### Der Beruf im Detail: Was macht eine Assistenzärztin?
Assistenzärztinnen und Assistenzärzte stehen mitten in der Patientenversorgung. Sie untersuchen, stellen Diagnosen, verordnen Therapien und führen die Visite mit. Dabei wachsen Sie unter Supervision erfahrener Kaderärzte Schritt für Schritt in mehr Verantwortung hinein – genau so ist die ärztliche Weiterbildung gedacht.

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life.

More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between.

Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.
Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com .
The Opportunity
Carrot is expanding its telemedicine clinic with a network of part-time, fully remote physician consultants who deliver evidence-based virtual care to members across multiple U.S. states. Depending on your licensure, certification, and area of expertise, you will provide consultations in menopause and perimenopause care aligned to The Menopause Society and ACOG guidelines, early fertility support aligned to ACOG and ASRM guidelines, or both.
Metabolic health is a core, cross-cutting component of this program. Weight, insulin resistance, and cardiometabolic risk are central to outcomes across every journey we support, from ovulatory function and preconception readiness to menopausal symptom burden and long-term cardiovascular and bone health.

You should expect metabolic assessment and management to be a routine part of your visits, and clinicians comfortable prescribing and managing anti-obesity medications, including GLP-1 receptor agonists, within clinical protocols are especially encouraged to apply.
This is a flexible, part-time contractor engagement of approximately 5-40 hours per week, with a target commitment of 10-15 hours per week.
What You’ll Own

Provide virtual consultations (video and/or phone) within your area(s) of expertise, including assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning, and ongoing management of menopausal, fertility, and related hormonal and metabolic concerns.
Apply current ACOG, ASRM, and The Menopause Society guidelines with individualized, shared decision-making.
Assess and manage metabolic health as a routine part of visits, including prescribing and managing anti-obesity medications such as GLP-1 receptor agonists within clinical protocols where appropriate.
Document visits accurately and on time, order and interpret relevant labs, and coordinate referrals to primary care, OB/GYN, endocrinology, behavioral health, or subspecialists as needed.
Maintain active, unrestricted multi-state clinical licensure, complete credentialing and payer enrollment, and maintain eligibility for additional state licenses to expand coverage.
Contribute to member experience and quality through strong virtual visit presence, effective use of telehealth and EHR systems, participation in chart audits and case reviews, and staying current with emerging research and regulatory changes.
What Success Looks Like

s.h: In your first 12–18 months, you will have
s.t:
Established a consistent panel of high-quality virtual visits within your clinical area(s), with strong member experience and visit quality results.
Maintained timely, accurate documentation and lab follow-up, with no outstanding credentialing or compliance gaps.
Expanded your state licensure coverage in line with program needs, supporting broader member access.
Integrated metabolic assessment and management, including GLP-1 protocols where clinically appropriate, as a routine part of your visits.
Contributed to chart audits, case reviews, and clinical protocol refinement as the telemedicine program scales.

An MD or DO in Obstetrics/Gynecology, Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility (REI), Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, or Endocrinology; or you are a Physician Assistant (PA) or Advanced Practice Registered Nurse/Nurse Practitioner (e.g., WHNP, adult/gerontology NP, FNP) with demonstrated expertise in the applicable clinical area.
A minimum of 3-5+ years of active clinical experience in early fertility support, menopause care, or both, including evaluation, treatment, and longitudinal management.
An active, unrestricted U.S. medical license; multi-state licensure is preferred and IMLC participation is strongly preferred.
For clinicians practicing in the menopause specialty: MSCP certification from The Menopause Society, or certification actively in progress with a clear completion plan.
Familiarity with ACOG, ASRM, and The Menopause Society guidelines.
Prior telemedicine experience (preferred), with comfort managing visits entirely in a virtual environment and a strong virtual presence that supports shared decision-making over video and phone.
Proficiency with telehealth technologies, including video platforms, secure messaging, electronic prescribing, and EHR/clinical documentation tools.
Familiarity with HIPAA and applicable telemedicine privacy, security, and regulatory requirements, along with a HIPAA-compliant home workspace and reliable internet.

s.h: While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring
s.t:
Clinical experience spanning both early fertility and menopause, enabling flexible coverage across member journeys.
Experience working in a dedicated menopause clinic, fertility center, or comparable specialty program.
Familiarity with early fertility workup, including AMH testing, ovulation induction, and preconception optimization, with appropriate escalation to in-person ART evaluation.
Experience prescribing and managing anti-obesity medications, including GLP-1 receptor agonists (titration, side-effect management, monitoring, and discontinuation planning); obesity medicine training or ABOM certification is a significant advantage.
Prior experience in digital health, health benefits, or multi-state telemedicine environments.
Experience contributing to clinical protocol development, quality improvement, or member-facing clinical content.
Experience supporting diverse and historically underserved populations, including LGBTQ+ and gender-diverse individuals.
Fluency in an additional language.
Why This Role Matters
Carrot's telemedicine clinic is one of the most direct ways members experience our care. Every virtual visit shapes how members navigate some of the most personal moments of their lives, from trying to conceive to managing menopause. The clinicians in this network are the face of that experience, and the quality of their judgment, communication, and documentation determines whether members receive care they trust.
This role also anchors Carrot's clinical point of view that metabolic health is inseparable from reproductive and hormonal health. As the telemedicine program scales across states and journeys, the clinicians who join this network will directly expand access to guideline-aligned, whole-person care for members who often cannot find it locally.

To qualify for this position, you must meet the basic requirements as well as any additional requirements (if applicable) listed in the job announcement. Applicants pending the completion of training or license requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met.

Currently employed physician(s) in VA who met the requirements for appointment under the previous qualification standard at the time of their initial appointment are deemed to have met the basic requirements of the occupation.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Degree of doctor of medicine or an equivalent degree resulting from a course of education in allopathic medicine or osteopathic medicine.

The degree must have been obtained from one of the schools approved by the Department of Veterans Affairs for the year in which the course of study was completed. Current, full and unrestricted license to practice medicine or surgery in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Residency Training: Physicians must have completed residency training, approved by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in an accredited core specialty training program leading to eligibility for board certification.

(NOTE: VA physicians involved in academic training programs may be required to be board certified for faculty status.) Approved residencies are: (1) Those approved by the accrediting bodies for graduate medical education, the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA), in the list published for the year the residency, or fellowship if applicable, was completed; OR (2) One year of post medical school training (internship, first year of residency, or transitional year residency) approved by ACGME or AOA followed by two years of post-training independent practice (performing under a full and unrestricted license) in the United States; OR (3) Non-US residency training programs followed by a minimum of three years of verified independent practice in the United States (performing under a full and unrestricted license) performing duties related to the position they are applying for (United States fellowships would be creditable towards this requirement), which the local Medical Staff Executive Committee deems to have provided the applicant with appropriate professional training and believes has exposed the Physician to an appropriate range of patient care experiences.

Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis. PRPs are not considered independent practitioners and will not be privileged; rather, they are to have a "scope of practice" that allows them to perform certain restricted duties under supervision.

Additionally, surgery residents in gap years may also be appointed as PRPs.

In rare and unusual circumstances, the Facility Director can submit a memo to the VISN Director through the VISN Chief Medical Officer, who may approve requests for reasonable exceptions to the residency training requirement for Physicians whose composite record of experience, accomplishments, performance, and qualifications warrant such action.

Description de l'entreprise
Premier réseau de soins intégrés de Suisse, le Réseau de l'Arc est un acteur de référence de la prise en charge coordonnée et de proximité, dans les domaines somatique et de la santé mentale. Comptant près de 1'300 collaborateurs, il s'appuie sur deux sites hospitaliers à Moutier et à Saint\-Imier ainsi que sur un réseau de Medicentres, de services ambulanciers, d'EMS, d'instituts de radiologie, d'un centre de thérapies physiques et cognitives et d'un service d'hospitalisation à domicile.
Le Réseau de l'Arc couvre les besoins médico\-hospitaliers d'une population de près de 80'000 habitants et se distingue par son dynamisme, ses excellentes infrastructures et sa volonté constante de développer des prestations de proximité et de qualité.
Notre service de gynécologie\-obstétrique du site de Saint\-Imier est en plein développement. Il réalise chaque année près de 600 interventions gynécologiques, en ambulatoire comme en stationnaire, et accompagne environ 400 naissances. Grâce à une équipe médicale expérimentée et engagée, nous offrons à nos patientes une prise en charge complète, humaine et de proximité.

Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. Exceptions: Residents currently enrolled in ACGME/AOA accredited residency training programs and who would otherwise meet the basic requirements for appointment are eligible to be appointed as "Physician Resident Providers" (PRPs).

PRPs must be fully licensed physicians (i.e., not a training license) and may only be appointed on an intermittent basis.
